title: Introduction to OSHA practice questions
description: Free Introduction to OSHA practice questions on 29 CFR 1903 and 1904. Every answer is explained and linked to the section it comes from.

questions.question: On construction work, which is a physically dispersed activity, where must the OSHA notice to employees be posted?

options.A: At the employer's corporate headquarters only
options.B: Inside each piece of heavy equipment
options.C: At the location to which employees report each day
options.D: On the employer's website

questions.explanation: For physically dispersed activities such as construction, the notice "shall be posted at the location to which employees report each day."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.2, Posting of notice; availability of the Act, regulations and applicable standards (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: When advance notice of an inspection is allowed, how far ahead may it be given, apart from apparent imminent danger and other unusual circumstances?

options.A: Not more than 24 hours before the inspection
options.B: Not more than 7 calendar days before
options.C: Not more than 15 working days before
options.D: Not more than 30 days before

questions.explanation: Advance notice "shall not be given more than 24 hours before the inspection is scheduled to be conducted, except in apparent imminent danger situations and in other unusual circumstances."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.6, Advance notice of inspections (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: The representative the employees have authorized for an inspection is not an employee of the employer. Under 1903.8(c), when may this third party accompany the Compliance Safety and Health Officer?

options.A: Never, because only employees may accompany the officer
options.B: Only with the employer's written consent
options.C: Only if the third party is a licensed attorney
options.D: When, in the officer's judgment, good cause has been shown that accompaniment by a third party is reasonably necessary to an effective and thorough physical inspection

questions.explanation: The authorized representative "may be an employee of the employer or a third party", and a non-employee may accompany the officer if, in the officer's judgment, "good cause has been shown why accompaniment by a third party is reasonably necessary to the conduct of an effective and thorough physical inspection of the workplace".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.8, Representatives of employers and employees (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: If an employer refuses to let the Compliance Safety and Health Officer enter, what does the officer do?

options.A: Issues an on-the-spot fine and enters anyway
options.B: Terminates the inspection or confines it to areas with no objection, and reports the refusal to the Area Director
options.C: Closes the job site until the employer agrees
options.D: Asks the local police to force entry

questions.explanation: The officer "shall terminate the inspection or confine the inspection to other areas" where no objection is raised, and "shall immediately report the refusal and the reason therefor to the Area Director."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.4, Objection to inspection (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An employee gives the Area Director notice of an alleged violation to request an inspection. What does 1903.11(a) require of that notice?

options.A: It must be notarized
options.B: It must be in writing, set forth the grounds with reasonable particularity, and be signed by the employee or representative of employees
options.C: It must be co-signed by the employer
options.D: It must be filed within 24 hours of noticing the hazard

questions.explanation: "Any such notice shall be reduced to writing, shall set forth with reasonable particularity the grounds for the notice, and shall be signed by the employee or representative of employees."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.11, Complaints by employees (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An inspection is made because of an employee complaint. What may the inspection cover?

options.A: Only the exact hazard named in the complaint
options.B: Only the area where the complaining employee works
options.C: Only records, not physical conditions
options.D: It is not limited to matters referred to in the complaint

questions.explanation: "Inspections under this section shall not be limited to matters referred to in the complaint."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.11, Complaints by employees (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: After an officer tells an employer about an imminent danger, the employer immediately eliminates the imminence of the danger and starts steps to abate it. What does 1903.13 say about citations?

options.A: Appropriate citations and notices of proposed penalties may still be issued
options.B: No citation may be issued once the danger is eliminated
options.C: Only a verbal warning may be given
options.D: A citation may be issued only if someone was injured

questions.explanation: "Appropriate citations and notices of proposed penalties may be issued with respect to an imminent danger even though, after being informed of such danger by the Compliance Safety and Health Officer, the employer immediately eliminates the imminence of the danger and initiates steps to abate such danger."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.13, Imminent danger (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: On the basis of an inspection, a Compliance Safety and Health Officer concludes that conditions could reasonably be expected to cause death or serious physical harm immediately or before the danger can be eliminated through the Act's other enforcement procedures. Whom must the officer inform?

options.A: Only the local fire department
options.B: Only the employer's insurance carrier
options.C: The affected employees and employers, telling them a civil action to restrain the conditions is being recommended
options.D: No one until the citation is mailed

questions.explanation: The officer "shall inform the affected employees and employers of the danger and that he is recommending a civil action to restrain such conditions or practices".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.13, Imminent danger (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Besides describing the alleged violation with particularity, what must every citation also fix under 1903.14(b)?

options.A: The date of the next inspection
options.B: The name of the employee who complained
options.C: The employer's insurance deductible
options.D: A reasonable time or times for the abatement of the alleged violation

questions.explanation: "Any citation shall also fix a reasonable time or times for the abatement of the alleged violation."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.14, Citations; notices of de minimis violations; policy regarding employee rescue activities (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An employer receives a notice of de minimis violations. What does 1903.16 say about posting it?

options.A: It need not be posted
options.B: It must be posted for 3 working days
options.C: It must be posted until April 30
options.D: It must be mailed to each employee instead

questions.explanation: Citations must be posted at or near each place of alleged violation, but "Notices of de minimis violations need not be posted."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.16, Posting of citations (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Where must an employer post a citation it receives, where that is practicable?

options.A: In the company's annual report
options.B: In the employer's main office files only
options.C: Unedited, at or near each place an alleged violation referred to in the citation occurred
options.D: On the OSHA 300 Log

questions.explanation: The employer "shall immediately post such citation, or a copy thereof, unedited, at or near each place an alleged violation referred to in the citation occurred".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.16, Posting of citations (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1903.17(a), what must every employer notice of intention to contest specify?

options.A: The name of the employer's attorney
options.B: Whether it is directed to the citation or to the proposed penalty, or both
options.C: The number of employees on the site
options.D: The date the hazard was abated

questions.explanation: "Every notice of intention to contest shall specify whether it is directed to the citation or to the proposed penalty, or both."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.17, Employer and employee contests before the Review Commission (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An employer posts its petition for modification of abatement date. Under 1903.14a(c)(2), within what time must affected employees or their representatives file a written objection to avoid waiving any further right to object?

options.A: Within ten (10) working days of the date of posting or service
options.B: Within 24 hours of the posting
options.C: Within 6 months of the posting
options.D: Within 30 calendar days of the original citation

questions.explanation: "Failure to file such objection within ten (10) working days of the date of posting of such petition or of service upon an authorized representative shall constitute a waiver of any further right to object to said petition."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.14a, Petitions for modification of abatement date (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An employer requests an informal conference about a citation. What effect does this have on the 15-working-day period to file a notice of contest?

options.A: It doubles the period to 30 working days
options.B: It pauses the period until the conference ends
options.C: It cancels the citation
options.D: It does not stay the 15-working-day period

questions.explanation: "No such conference or request for such conference shall operate as a stay of any 15-working-day period for filing a notice of intention to contest".

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.20, Informal conferences (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: What deadline does 1903.19 set for an employer to certify to OSHA that a cited violation has been abated, unless the compliance officer observed the abatement during the on-site inspection within 24 hours after the violation was identified and noted it in the citation?

options.A: Before the closing conference
options.B: Within 24 hours of receiving the citation
options.C: Within 10 calendar days after the abatement date
options.D: At the end of the calendar year

questions.explanation: "Within 10 calendar days after the abatement date, the employer must certify to OSHA (the Agency) that each cited violation has been abated," except as provided in paragraph (c)(2).

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1903.19, Abatement verification (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: A company had 10 or fewer employees at all times during the last calendar year, and neither OSHA nor the Bureau of Labor Statistics has informed it in writing that it must keep records. What does Part 1904 require?

options.A: It must keep full OSHA 300, 300-A and 301 records
options.B: It need not keep OSHA injury and illness records, but must still report fatalities, in-patient hospitalizations, amputations and eye losses
options.C: It is exempt from all of Part 1904, including reporting
options.D: It must keep records only for supervisors

questions.explanation: Such a company does "not need to keep OSHA injury and illness records unless OSHA or the Bureau of Labor Statistics informs you in writing", but all covered employers "must report to OSHA any work-related incident that results in a fatality, the in-patient hospitalization of one or more employees, an employee amputation, or an employee loss of an eye."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.1, Partial exemption for employers with 10 or fewer employees (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An employee is cut by a sharp object contaminated with another person's blood, and the case is recordable. What does 1904.29 say about the employee's name on the OSHA 300 Log?

options.A: It may not be entered, because this is a privacy concern case
options.B: It must be entered in full so the case can be tracked
options.C: Only the employee's initials are entered
options.D: The employee's badge number replaces it

questions.explanation: Cuts from sharp objects "that are contaminated with another person's blood or other potentially infectious material" are privacy concern cases, and for those "you may not enter the employee's name on the OSHA 300 Log." The words privacy case go in the space normally used for the name.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.29, Forms (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Which person does 1904.32(b)(4) list as a company executive who may certify the annual summary?

options.A: The chair of the site safety committee
options.B: Any first-line supervisor
options.C: The company's outside accountant
options.D: The highest ranking company official working at the establishment

questions.explanation: The certifying company executive must be an owner (sole proprietorship or partnership only), an officer of the corporation, "The highest ranking company official working at the establishment", or that official's immediate supervisor.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.32, Annual summary (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: During the five-year storage period, which stored record must the employer update to include newly discovered recordable injuries or illnesses?

options.A: The annual summary only
options.B: The OSHA 300 Logs
options.C: The OSHA 301 Incident Reports only
options.D: None, because stored records may not be changed

questions.explanation: During the storage period "you must update your stored OSHA 300 Logs to include newly discovered recordable injuries or illnesses"; updating the annual summary and the 301 Incident Reports is not required.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.33, Retention and updating (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: An employer must report an employee's work-related in-patient hospitalization, and the nearest OSHA Area Office is closed. Which way of reporting does 1904.39 accept?

options.A: Leaving a message on the Area Office answering machine
options.B: Faxing the Area Office
options.C: Using the 800 number or the reporting application on OSHA's public Web site
options.D: Sending an email to the Area Office

questions.explanation: "No, if the Area Office is closed, you must report the fatality, in-patient hospitalization, amputation, or loss of an eye using either the 800 number or the reporting application located on OSHA's public Web site at www.osha.gov."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1904.39, Reporting fatalities, hospitalizations, amputations, and losses of an eye as a result of work-related incidents to OSHA (as of Nov 3, 2026)
